description: Create a draft: a title and one variant per account, each with its own text and media. Nothing is sent. Answers the draft with its id and version. Check it with drafts_validate and show it to the user before publish or schedule. A TikTok post also waits for the owner: TikTok has them choose, on a screen of ours, who can see each video, whether people may comment, duet or stitch, and whether it promotes a brand. Those choices cannot be sent here. When a draft has a TikTok account, the answer carries choose: one { accountId, network, link } per TikTok account still waiting; hand the user that link and wait for them to make the choices there (they can post from that screen too).

brandId.description: The brand this is for, by its id from brands_list. Needed when the login has more than one brand; with one brand it can be left out.

title.description: A name for the draft in the user’s own list. It is never posted.

variants.description: One entry per account the post goes to, each with its own text and media.

kind.description: Leave out for an ordinary post. "story" sends exactly one photo or video as an Instagram or Facebook story, with empty text.

mediaIds.description: Media ids from media_upload, media_list or templates_render, in the order they should appear. Empty for a text post.

options.description: What a post carries besides its text and media, on the eight networks that take it; leave out everywhere else. Instagram: collaborators, tags (a story takes tags only), firstReply, aiGenerated, and for a reel cover, reelsOnly and trial. Facebook Pages: firstReply (not a story). LinkedIn: firstReply. Threads: firstReply, threadPosts, quotePostId and replyToId. YouTube: visibility, videoTags, containsSyntheticMedia and publishAt. Pinterest: board, link and cover. X: thread, firstReply and threadPosts. Google Business Profile: type, language, button, title, start, end and offer. Not TikTok: who can see a TikTok video and how people may interact with it are chosen by the owner on the TikTok screen (the link in choose), never here.

aiGenerated.description: Instagram only (not a story): true labels the photo, reel or carousel as AI-generated media.

board.description: Pinterest only: the board this pin goes to, by its name as shown on Pinterest or its id (boards_list lists them). Left out, the pin goes to the account’s chosen board.

button.description: One button on an update or an event. An offer has none.

action.description: What the button says. "call" rings the phone number on the profile.

url.description: Where the button leads, starting with https://. Leave out for "call".

collaborators.description: Instagram only: up to 3 Instagram usernames invited to share the post, so it shows on their profile too once they accept. A photo, a reel or a carousel; not a story. Ask the user who; never guess a username.

containsSyntheticMedia.description: YouTube only: true or false declaring whether the video contains altered or AI-generated realistic content.

cover.description: Pinterest and Instagram, a video: the whole second whose frame is its cover, such as 3. On Instagram for a reel (one video on its own).

end.description: The last day, written the same way as start. Give a time for both or for neither.

firstReply.description: X, Threads, LinkedIn, Instagram and Facebook Pages (not stories): the text of a first comment or reply posted right under the post. Ideal for links without hurting reach. Limits: 280 weighted characters on X, 500 on Threads, 1250 on LinkedIn, 2200 on Instagram and Facebook Pages. On X with thread, it rides on the first reply with the second picture.

language.description: The language the post is written in, as a code such as en or es.

link.description: Pinterest only: the https address the pin leads to, such as a page of the business’s website. Left out, the first https address in the description is used.

offer.description: An offer only: what the customer needs to redeem it.

code.description: The code a customer gives, up to 58 characters.

url.description: Where the offer is redeemed online, starting with https://.

publishAt.description: YouTube only: future ISO 8601 timestamp with timezone (such as 2026-12-01T14:00:00Z) for native YouTube scheduled publishing. Keeps the video private until then; requires visibility to be "private" or omitted.

quotePostId.description: Threads only: numeric Threads post id to quote in this post.

reelsOnly.description: Instagram only, a reel: true shows it in the Reels tab only, not in the feed.

replyToId.description: Threads only: numeric Threads post id to reply to.

start.description: The first day of the offer or event, as YYYY-MM-DD, or with a time as YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM, in the business’s own local time. Needed for both.

tags.description: Instagram only: people tagged, up to 20 on each photo or video. On a photo give x and y, the spot where the person is; on a video leave them out; on a story they are optional. Ask the user who; never guess a username.

file.description: Which photo or video the tag is on: 1 is the first (the default).

username.description: The Instagram username of the person tagged.

x.description: Where on the photo, from 0 (left edge) to 1 (right edge).

y.description: Where on the photo, from 0 (top edge) to 1 (bottom edge).

thread.description: X only: true posts the pictures as a thread, the first on the post with its text and each next one on a reply of its own, up to 10. X crops several pictures on one post into small tiles, so a carousel goes to X this way, drawn in the landscape cut (templates_render).

threadPosts.description: X and Threads: 1 to 24 follow-up text posts chained as replies under the main post (up to 280 weighted characters each on X, up to 500 characters each on Threads).

title.description: The name of the offer or event, up to 58 characters. Needed for both.

trial.description: Instagram only, a reel: post it as a trial reel, shown to non-followers first. "manual": the owner shares it with followers in Instagram; "auto": Instagram shares it when it does well. Ask the user.

videoTags.description: YouTube only: 1 to 30 keyword tags for the video, up to 500 combined characters, without < or >.

visibility.description: YouTube only: who can see this video, chosen by the user for each upload (YouTube asks that they can). Ask them; until it is set, drafts_validate and the draft list it under ask, and it goes up as public.

text.description: The caption for this account, within that network’s limit (see capabilities). Empty for a story. On YouTube the first line is the video title.

name: drafts_create
title: Write a draft
